border.note: Alpha rather than solid so one token works over any surface.

bg-hover.note: The only hover treatment in the system.

scrim.note: Dims SoundCloud behind a modal surface. Always paired with the Overlay shadow.

title.purpose: Settings panel heading. The largest text in the entire product.

body.purpose: Setting names — the primary reading size in the panel.

label.purpose: Navigation items, inputs and selects. The dense working tier.

caption.purpose: Help text under a setting, and the window title in the chrome strip.

overline.purpose: One use only: the NOT IMPLEMENTED YET badge on a pending setting.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. A wide ambient layer plus a tight contact layer, used exclusively when a surface floats above the app and takes over input. Always paired with the scrim.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Settings panel entrance: 14px upward fly plus fade, with the scrim fading over the same duration. Exit reverses it.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the duration collapses to zero rather than substituting a different animation.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hover states are instant. The wash appears on the frame it is needed; no transition.

breakpoints.name: panel-min
breakpoints.purpose: Below this window width the settings card stops being 760px wide and falls back to 100% - 48px.

breakpoints.name: window-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum window width enforced by BaseWindow; the chrome is not designed below it.

components.name: Chrome Button
components.description: The signature control. Transparent until hovered, 30x26px, sized for a 32px strip.
components.css: .ds-btn-chrome { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 30px; height: 26px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: var(--bsc-radius, 6px); background: transparent; color: var(--bsc-text-primary, #1a1a1a); cursor: default; } .ds-btn-chrome:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--bsc-bg-hover, rgb(0 0 0 / 8%)); } .ds-btn-chrome:disabled { color: var(--bsc-text-disabled, #a8a8a8); } .ds-btn-chrome:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--bsc-accent, #f50); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-btn-chrome svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; fill: none; stroke: currentcolor; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }

components.description: The one saturated moment in the product: hover fills Danger Red with a white glyph.

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: Settings rail item. Selection is carried by weight and ink, not by colour.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; width: 160px; padding: 12px 8px; border-right: 1px solid var(--bsc-border, rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)); } .ds-nav-item { padding: 8px 10px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--bsc-radius, 6px); background: transparent; color: var(--bsc-text-secondary, #5c5c5c); font: inherit; font-size: 13px; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--bsc-bg-hover, rgb(0 0 0 / 8%)); } .ds-nav-item--active { background: var(--bsc-bg-hover, rgb(0 0 0 / 8%)); color: var(--bsc-text-primary, #1a1a1a); font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--bsc-accent, #f50); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Field
components.description: Text input and select. Field White on Shell Grey so the control reads as inset.
components.css: .ds-field { min-width: 140px; padding: 6px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--bsc-border, rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)); border-radius: var(--bsc-radius, 6px); background: var(--bsc-bg-secondary, #fff); color: var(--bsc-text-primary, #1a1a1a); font: inherit; font-size: 13px; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--bsc-accent, #f50); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-field:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Native 16px control with accent-color set to SoundCloud Orange — the second and last place the accent appears.
components.css: .ds-checkbox { width: 16px; height: 16px; accent-color: var(--bsc-accent, #f50); } .ds-checkbox:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-checkbox:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--bsc-accent, #f50); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.description: The only surface in the system that floats. Scrim plus two-layer shadow arrive together as one modality signal.

Flat at rest. Depth means modality.
components.css: .ds-overlay { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 260px; padding: 24px; background: var(--bsc-scrim, rgb(0 0 0 / 45%)); } .ds-card { width: min(420px, 100%); overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--bsc-border, rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--bsc-bg-primary, #f2f2f2); box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgb(0 0 0 / 35%), 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 20%); } .ds-card-header { padding: 10px 12px 10px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bsc-border, rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)); } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--bsc-text-primary, #1a1a1a); } .ds-card-body { padding: 16px 20px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--bsc-text-secondary, #5c5c5c); }

narrative.overview:
BetterSoundCloud is a frame around someone else's picture. SoundCloud's own web app renders every piece of music UI — the player, the waveforms, the artwork, the navigation — inside a content view that this design system deliberately never touches. What we own is a 32px strip along the top, a settings panel that floats over it, and future overlays. That is the entire canvas, and the frame's job is to hold the picture without competing with it.

This produces a system that is almost aggressively restrained. There is no display type, no hero, no imagery, no gradient, and no decorative colour anywhere. Controls are transparent until you hover them. The largest text in the product is 15px. The accent appears only where something is focused, selected, or on. A user should be able to look at this app all day and never notice the chrome — and then find every control exactly where they left it the moment they reach for one.

The restraint is architectural before it is aesthetic. Our chrome lives outside SoundCloud's document precisely so their releases cannot break it, and that same separation is why the frame must not imitate their surface language: two competing music UIs stacked in one window would read as a skin, not a client. Depth follows the same logic — surfaces are flat and separated by hairline borders, and a shadow appears only when something floats above the app and takes over input.
keyCharacteristics: One 32px chrome strip; nothing else is permanently on screen
Flat at rest — borders separate, shadows signal modality
Two radii, two shadows, one type family, one accent
Controls invisible until hovered; icons are 15px stroked outlines
Every colour defined twice, light and dark, and never hard-coded outside the token file
Honesty rendered visually: unbuilt features appear disabled and labelled, never functional-looking

rules.name: The Borrowed Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is SoundCloud's, not ours. It marks state — focused, selected, on — and never decorates. If orange appears somewhere that is not a state, remove it.

rules.name: The Two-Mode Rule
rules.body: Every colour exists twice and is consumed only through a --bsc-* custom property. A literal hex outside tokens.css is a bug: it will be correct in one mode and wrong in the other. The single sanctioned exception is #fff on the danger hover, which must stay white in both modes.

rules.name: The 15px Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing in BetterSoundCloud's own UI is larger than 15px. The frame has no headlines because the frame has nothing to announce. If a surface seems to need display type, it probably belongs to SoundCloud's view, not ours.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: No webfonts, ever. The chrome inherits the OS UI font so it belongs to the window; the CSP on every renderer blocks remote font loads regardless.

rules.name: The 32px Rule
rules.body: The chrome is 32px and never grows. Every new affordance either fits in that strip, moves into settings, or becomes an overlay. Growing the frame steals from the picture.

rules.name: The Modality Rule
rules.body: Shadow is not decoration and not hierarchy — it means 'this has taken over input'. A surface that does not block interaction does not get a shadow. If you reach for elevation to make something look important, use a border and a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 6px for anything you interact with, 10px for anything that floats. A third radius is a new concept — justify it or drop it.

dos: Do consume colour through --bsc-* custom properties, so every surface works in both modes.
Do keep the accent to state only — focus rings and selection. Its rarity is what makes it legible.
Do separate surfaces with 1px Hairline borders and the single tonal step, not with shadow.
Do pair the scrim and the Overlay shadow whenever something takes over input, and use neither otherwise.
Do give every new control a visible focus state (2px accent outline, outline-offset: -2px) and full keyboard operability — the product targets WCAG 2.2 AA for its own chrome.
Do render an unbuilt capability as a disabled control with the NOT IMPLEMENTED YET badge rather than hiding it or letting it appear functional.
Do expose stable data-bsc-* attributes on themable regions, and treat tokens.css plus those attributes as the versioned public API for user themes.
donts: Don't target Svelte's generated hash classes (.s-050uw8y64xWw) from a theme. They change every build. That is what the data-bsc-* attributes exist for.
Don't build a generic Electron dashboard — Material-style cards, elevation for its own sake, an icon rail, dense chrome competing with the content it wraps. Confirmed anti-reference.

Don't adopt consumer music-app surface language — gradient heroes, artwork bleeding into blurred backgrounds, oversized transport controls. SoundCloud already renders all of that one layer below; duplicating it makes the client a skin. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop blur, glow, or saturated gradients. They read as a theme rather than a tool and destroy legibility in a 32px strip. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't introduce a webfont. The CSP blocks remote loads, and the OS stack is the point.
Don't add a third radius, a second shadow, or a second accent without retiring one first.
Don't exceed 15px type in BetterSoundCloud's own UI.
Don't grow the chrome past 32px. New affordances go into settings or an overlay.
Don't style SoundCloud's page from a component stylesheet. Page-level appearance is CSS-only through insertCSS, and no node may be added to their document.
